key_insight: Deep learning of retinal fluorescence lifetime maps modestly distinguished type 2 diabetes status, outperforming an age-only classifier.
clinical_relevance: FLIO may capture diabetes-associated retinal metabolic signals, but these results do not establish a clinically reliable screening or diagnostic tool.
method: Analyzed FLIO scans from 1,783 AI-READI participants grouped as normoglycemic, prediabetic, or diabetic.
Generated corrected center-of-mass mean fluorescence lifetime maps and tested group differences with age adjustment.
Evaluated CNN, ResNet-18, and XGBoost classifiers against age-only and FLIO-plus-age models.
evidence_signal: The FLIO CNN achieved AUROC 0.60 ± 0.04 for three-class classification versus 0.51 ± 0.03 for age alone, and 0.67 ± 0.04 for normal versus diabetic classification.
watch_item: Modest discrimination in this cross-sectional dataset warrants independent validation before clinical use.
paper_title: Deep Learning of Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Ophthalmoscopy for Type 2 Diabetes Classification
